body.statement: For every canonically encoded fixed instance \(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K\) satisfying the model assumptions, let \(F\) be the dense polynomial obtained by replaying its target factorization. There exist serialized endpoint groundings \(Z\) and a certificate \(Gamma\) such that \(Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,Gamma)=1\). The combined bit length of \(Z\) and \(Gamma\), and the checker's bit running time on the complete input and certificate, are bounded by one fixed polynomial in \(D+LF+T+1\). Each selected optimizer and endpoint is represented by a primitive irreducible integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval, and its algebraic degree is at most \(\max\{1,D-1\}\).
body.justification: Completeness and an input-based size bound prevent the grammar from achieving soundness by refusing hard legal instances or hiding exponential proof objects.
body.gap: Exact root-isolation papers bound algebraic certificates for supplied polynomials, but the polynomial-size composition with value links, tie handling, and relational model tables is not supplied by the causal or verification literature.
body.consumer: A traffic-bound producer can always emit a finite replayable record whose checking cost is controlled by the explicit instance rather than by trust in neural or numerical optimization.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 N=D+LF+T+1.
\]
We construct \(Z\) and \(\Gamma\), show directly that every branch of the
checker accepts, and then bound the construction and verification costs.

Copy the canonical fixed-instance fields, the exhaustive \(Ictx\), and
the supported rational rows into the certificate.  Their length is
\(O(T+LF)\).  The hypothesis that \(F\) is obtained by replaying the
target factorization supplies an ordered list of the additions and
multiplications indexed by the explicit records of \(Ictx\).  Record this
list and its dense intermediate outputs.  There are only polynomially many
gates in the explicit incidence length.  In a product, numerator and
denominator bit lengths add.  In a sum of explicitly many terms, a common
denominator may be chosen as the product of their denominators, so its bit
length is the sum of their bit lengths, and the extra numerator growth is
at most logarithmic in the number of summands plus that denominator
length.  Degrees never exceed the explicitly counted occurrence degree
\(D\).  Hence every recorded rational coefficient has bit length
polynomial in \(N\), and exact gate replay ends at the supplied dense list
\(F\).

Choose \(M>0\) and a primitive \(A\in\mathbb Z[q]\) such that
\[
 F(q)=\frac{A(q)}{M}.
\]
Taking the product of the denominators in the dense input list before
primitive reduction shows that the coefficient bit length \(\tau\) of
\(A\), as well as \(\log M\), is polynomial in \(LF+D+1\).  If \(D=0\),
use the boundary-only candidate record, choose
\(qminus=qplus=0\), and put \(L=U=F(0)\).  If \(D=1\), \(F'\) is a
nonzero constant and the two boundary candidates suffice.  All selected
numbers in these cases have linear integer descriptors and rational
isolators.

Now suppose \(D\geq2\).  Compute the square-free part
\[
 g=\operatorname{sqfree}(A')
\]
by fraction-free gcd arithmetic.  The subresultant coefficients involved
are determinants of matrices of dimension \(O(D)\).  The determinant
expansion bounds their bit lengths by a polynomial in \(D+\tau+1\), so
\(g\) has degree at most \(D-1\), polynomial coefficient length, and is
computable in polynomial bit time.  By
\(\texttt{lem:integer-root-isolation-polynomial-time}\), one can compute
pairwise disjoint polynomial-length rational isolators for all real roots
of \(g\) in polynomial bit time.  Exact Sturm counts retain precisely
those in \((0,1)\), and the boundary records add \(0\) and \(1\).
Repeated roots of \(A'\) occur once because \(g\) is square free.

Apply
\(\texttt{lem:rational-polynomial-factorization-polynomial-time}\) to
\(g\).  For each retained interior root, attach the primitive irreducible
integer factor having the isolated root.  The factor together with its
rational isolator is an exact simple-extension representation of the
candidate and has polynomial bit length.

Introduce an indeterminate value \(z\) and form
\[
 E(z)
 =(Mz-A(0))(Mz-A(1))
   \operatorname{Res}_{q}\!\left(g(q),A(q)-Mz\right).
\]
The resultant factor is nonzero: over \(\mathbb Q(z)\), a common divisor
of \(g(q)\) and \(A(q)-Mz\) would have to divide the nonzero coefficient
\(-M\) of \(z\), and hence would be a unit.  Its Sylvester matrix has
dimension \(O(D)\), entries of \(z\)-degree at most one, and coefficient
bit length polynomial in \(D+\tau+1\).  Determinant expansion therefore
gives
\[
 \deg E\leq D+1
\]
and polynomial coefficient bit length.  Primitive and square-free
reduction preserve polynomial degree and coefficient size by the same
subresultant determinant bounds.

Isolate every distinct real root of the square-free part of \(E\), again
using
\(\texttt{lem:integer-root-isolation-polynomial-time}\).  For an interior
candidate \(c\), regard \(A(c)-Mz\) as a linear polynomial in \(z\) over
\(\mathbb Q(c)\).  The algorithm in
\(\texttt{lem:algebraic-extension-isolation-polynomial-time}\) isolates
its unique root \(F(c)\) in bit time polynomial in the displayed input
degrees and coefficient lengths.  Equality with a rational endpoint
\(\ell\) is decided exactly by reducing \(A(c)-M\ell\) modulo the attached
irreducible polynomial of \(c\); otherwise sign-guided refinement decides
the strict side.  Refine until exactly one value-root interval
\(J=(\ell,u)\) satisfies
\[
 \ell<F(c)<u.
\]
Such an interval exists because, after specializing the Sylvester matrix
at \(z=F(c)\), the shared root \(c\) supplies a nonzero kernel vector and
therefore \(E(F(c))=0\).  It is unique because the square-free value-root
intervals are disjoint and have count one.  Evaluate boundary candidates
by rational arithmetic and link them in the same list.

Candidates have equal values exactly when their exact links identify the
same root of the square-free value polynomial; otherwise their disjoint
isolators give a strict order after refinement.  Assign one label per
equal-value class and sort those labels.  This handles ties without
attempting to separate equal numerical intervals.  It also ensures that
an extraneous real resultant root with no feasible candidate link is
never selected.  The least and greatest linked labels determine
\(L,U,qminus,qplus\).  Sturm--Tarski sign records serialize each link,
tie, and strict comparison in the grammar of
\(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\).

Factor the square-free value polynomial and retain for each selected
endpoint the primitive irreducible factor containing its one-root
isolator.  An interior optimizer \(q_\circ\) is a root of \(A'\), so
\[
 [\mathbb Q(q_\circ):\mathbb Q]\leq D-1.
\]
Moreover \(F(q_\circ)=A(q_\circ)/M\) belongs to
\(\mathbb Q(q_\circ)\), whence
\[
 [\mathbb Q(F(q_\circ)):\mathbb Q]\leq D-1.
\]
Boundary optimizers and values are rational.  Thus each selected optimizer
and endpoint has algebraic degree at most
\(\max\{1,D-1\}\), with a primitive irreducible polynomial and rational
isolating interval as required.

Construct the two endpoint models by
\(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\).  If type \(t\) has \(R_t\) explicit
contexts and alphabet size \(k_t\), its number of positive atoms is at
most \(1+R_t(k_t-1)\).  Because the canonical explicit input lists all
these rows,
\[
 \sum_t R_t k_t=O(T).
\]
Consequently the number of entries in the context-by-atom mechanism
tables is at most
\[
 \sum_t R_t\bigl(1+R_t(k_t-1)\bigr)=O(T^2),
\]
and the source and target node references add \(O(T)\) entries.  Every
supported breakpoint is rational with description length bounded by the
input.  Per endpoint and type, the only possibly irrational adjacent
masses are \(q_\circ-a\) and \(b-q_\circ\), and they reference the single
polynomial-and-isolator descriptor already stored for \(q_\circ\).
Extension-field signs compare \(q_\circ\) with every rational threshold
and certify mass nonnegativity, including equality at a threshold.
Therefore \(Z\) has polynomial bit length and can be produced in
polynomial bit time.

Complete \(\Gamma\) with the canonical length-delimited digest, local
incidence records, exact gate identities, gcd and square-free identities,
Sturm counts, candidate-to-value links, tie labels, order records, and
exact source and target evaluations of the two finite models.  There are
at most \(D-1\) interior candidates, two boundary candidates, and at most
\(D+1\) distinct roots of the displayed value polynomial.  Even recording
all pairwise comparisons uses only \(O(D^2)\) records.  Every integer,
rational interval, polynomial, table, and arithmetic identity in these
records has bit length polynomial in \(N\), by the preceding determinant
bounds and the three cited polynomial-time algebraic algorithms.  Hence
\[
 |Z|+|\Gamma|\leq P(N)
\]
for one fixed polynomial \(P\).

It remains to prove acceptance rather than infer it circularly from
soundness.  On the constructed record, the digest matches by canonical
encoding; the copied incidence list is exhaustive; positive source
contexts and the rows in \(K\) agree by the instance hypothesis; the
recorded arithmetic replay ends at \(F\); the gcd, Sturm, resultant,
factor, isolator, link, tie, and ordering identities hold by their
construction; and the breakpoint models reproduce \(Psrc\) and evaluate
to \(L,U\) by \(\texttt{thm:endpoint-models}\).  Thus, on unfolding
\(\texttt{def:checker}\), every rejection guard is false and
\[
 Check(S,G,Rsrc,Psrc,\rho,a,B,Ictx,K,F,Z,\Gamma)=1.
\]
The checker traverses only polynomially many records.  Its rational
arithmetic, fraction-free gcd and resultant verification, Sturm
variations, factor and algebraic sign checks, table traversal, and
finite-model evaluations involve polynomially many integers of
polynomial bit length.  Standard bit arithmetic therefore bounds its
running time by another fixed polynomial in \(N\).  The sum of the two
bounding polynomials is one fixed polynomial bounding both quantities.
This proves certificate existence, the combined size bound, the
checking-time bound, and the algebraic-degree assertion.
